findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:713-717 checks only retained.role and retained.policy == _retention_policy(route). The design says the archive gate accepts the retained execution 'by the same policy equality check', so execution.retained.owner_approval is never required or compared with execution_plan.owner_approval. _validate_execution_plan covers only the plan. An execution record that omits or alters the approval still passes the archive gate.
findings.summary: The archive gate accepts an owner-approved retained execution without checking that execution.retained carries the owner_approval.

findings.evidence: approve_supervisor_diff (model_routing.py, about line 1136) only checks that the strings are non-empty. design.md Risks acknowledges this, so the only safeguard is documentation. This reopens the late-legalization path that the v1.9.0 gate closed, and the early gate now points agents to the command in its own error message.
findings.summary: Any agent can call the command with a free-text --approval, and nothing ties the record to a real owner decision.
